Phenotypes_info: Enzymes associated with arabinoxylan degradation, pentose metabolism, or short chain fatty acid (SCFA) production
Title: Xylanase Supplementation Modulates the Microbiota of the Large Intestine of Pigs Fed Corn-Based Fiber by Means of a Stimbiotic Mechanism of Action
Description: This research tested the hypothesis that xylanase modulates microbial communities within the large intestine of growing pigs fed corn-based fiber through a stimbiotic mechanism(s) of action (MOA). Sixty gilts were blocked by initial body weight, individually housed, and randomly assigned to one of four dietary treatments (n = 15): a low-fiber (LF) control, a high-fiber (HF) control containing 30% corn bran, HF+100 mg/kg xylanase (HF+XY), and HF+50 mg/kg arabinoxylan-oligosaccharide (HF+AX). Pigs were fed dietary treatments for 46 days. On day 46, pigs were euthanized, and mucosa and lumen contents were collected from the cecum and the colon.
